movie_title: The real reason polio is so dangerous
introduction: Explore what makes polio so dangerous, what is causing the 21st century resurgence of cases, and how
lead_intro: Discover the fascinating history and ongoing battle against polio in this informative video. Join us to explore the challenges faced by researchers in eradicating this deadly disease.

quiz.question: What is the main source of recent spikes in polio cases?
quiz.explanation: Recent spikes in polio cases are primarily due to the mutation of the poliovirus strains, leading to the emergence of new vaccine-derived strains in under-vaccinated populations.

quiz.question: What percentage of a community needs to be vaccinated to prevent strains from mutating?
quiz.explanation: At least 80% of every community needs to be vaccinated to prevent strains of poliovirus from mutating into new vaccine-derived strains.

quiz.question: What did US physician Jonas Salk develop in the early 1950s to combat polio?
quiz.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV) that prevented all three strains of poliovirus from causing paralysis when injected.

quiz.question: What role do monovalent and bivalent OPVs play in eradicating polio?
quiz.explanation: Monovalent and bivalent OPVs respectively contain one or two types of attenuated poliovirus, reducing the number of strains that could mutate and aiding in the eradication of polio.

quiz.question: What technology is being used to ensure populations meet vaccination thresholds?
quiz.explanation: Medical workers are using geospatial imaging and analysis to locate and immunize remote communities, ensuring that vaccination thresholds are met to prevent polio outbreaks.
